heldout_input_noise.note: mean squared residual / input sigma^2 (file sigma x load-time factors; no learned floor or noise scale), own mask, held-out exposures

approximations: F1 sky is static: s(Omega, lambda, t) = s(Omega, lambda) (no variable sources); spectrum = --spec-k (12) RBF bumps uniform in log lambda on the spectral domain (0.70-5.30 um, widened to cover every loaded filter's quadrature nodes by --spectral-domain union; K grows with the span only with --spec-k-rule span) (partition of unity, v40 basis without the learned correction): bump spacing 0.08 dex at K = 12 over the reference domain

F2 sky in space = tent (bilinear) interpolant of a coefficient grid at --sky-pitch over the box + 2 x --sky-margin; ZERO outside: sources outside the sky domain and their wings are absent; data are used only inside the box + 2 x --data-margin (< the sky margin)

F3 sky optimisation: fixed diagonal preconditioner 1 + f min(S/N_warm, cap) (5x5 dilated) on the coefficients; soft positivity penalty --sky-neg on the band images (in units of the band noise); TV off by default; warm start = inverse-variance bilinear splat of the training pixels at header-WCS (+ initial registration) positions, mapped to coefficients by v40's ridge spectral_init (PSF-blurred start)

F4 lambda integral: Q equal-weight nodes at the mid-quantiles of T(lambda)/lambda over the filter support (T >= 1e-3 max) of the PUBLISHED curve; exp(gamma) is evaluated at the nodes only; error vs Q measured in tests/test_fieldop_render.py

F5 kernel frame: v = R_e^T u with R_e the polar rotation (with parity) of the exposure's MEAN header Jacobian; the variation of the local WCS rotation/skew across the detector is left to the learned spatial code; the level grids are axis-aligned on the sky

F6 kernel field: FiLM MLP (--k-layers x --k-hidden) on a smooth log-radius encoding (core r0 = half the finest render pitch, radial Fourier frequencies 1..--enc-nrad over [r0, extent]) and angular harmonics m <= --enc-mmax (12: features narrower than ~15 deg in azimuth, e.g. thin diffraction spikes far out, are smoothed); log density clamped at 30
F7 unit integral of k on each renderer's OWN quadrature (FFT levels or per-pixel points); amplitude 'free' skips it (integral learned)

F8 code h additive in code space; hdet / hep centred and rms-normalised over reference sets (training detectors x 3x3 lattice; training epochs), recomputed every step; a code-space tau is not identifiable on its own (the field can rescale its sensitivity), so the output-space effective variability is reported next to it; the chromatic term tau_lam (hbar(lambda) - hbar(lambda_pivot)) is not normalised
F9 kernel truncated by a C1 taper between 0.85 and 1.0 x --kernel-extent; nothing beyond

F10 FFT kernel quadrature = nested square level grids (pitch p_r f^l, (2 n_h + 1)^2 nodes) with a C1 partition of unity in r (hand-over between a R_l and R_l); measured against the per-pixel quadrature (tests)
F11 training renders shift the level-0 grid by a random sub-pitch phase (--render-jitter) so that the field is learned as a continuous function; prediction uses phase 0
F12 levels with pitch >= 2 sky pixels read the box average of the COEFFICIENTS (not of the tent function); finer levels read the tent sky exactly
F13 correlated level images are read at the pixel positions by prefiltered cubic B-splines (periodic prefilter, valid inside the n_h + 3 margin) or Keys bicubic (--interp keys); error measured

F14 spatial variation inside a region: K evaluated at region nodes (lattice of --region-px per detector), correlated images blended with bilinear weights (= kernel interpolated bilinearly in xi); error vs region size measured

F15 pixel area alpha (--input-level rate) = |det((I + M_e)(J_wcs + dD/dxi))| with J_wcs from central differences of the per-pixel header positions (one-sided at the cut edges) and dD/dxi by 1-px central differences; the per-filter photometric conversion of _rate data is NOT an input yet, so in rate mode the sky has per-filter units; predictions of rate-trained models are in DN/s (not scorable against _cal)

F16 throughput log g: filter-level MLP of (lambda, filter input, instrument) + detector field (MLP of 2 Fourier frequencies of xi: no structure finer than ~1/4 detector) + epoch field, both normalised over their references (detector field: over the (detector, lambda node) pairs observed in training), + per-exposure gain random effect u_e ~ N(0, 1)

F17 throughput gauge (exact): the T-weighted mean of gamma over the reference set (training exposures; --gauge-ref-inst) evaluated on a 3x3 lattice per exposure is subtracted at every lambda node: the mean g of the reference set equals the published curves AT THE NODES; wavelengths not covered by the reference set get no condition

F18 gauges besides throughput: (a) COMMON BLUR, hard reparametrisation: every kernel is evaluated at v / s with s = sqrt(max(1, floor / M_ref)) (two fixed-point passes), M_ref = core second moment (Gaussian window of width 2 sqrt(floor)) of the mean kernel of the sharpest kernel class (filter with the smallest generic width (0.42 lambda/D)^2 + p^2/12) averaged over its lambda nodes, floor = --blur-floor x pitch^2 / 3 (one sky tent): no kernel class can be sharper than the sky grid supports; above the floor the blur is free (a common dilation is a reparametrisation, not the exact convolution gauge); (b) PEDESTAL: per filter, sum over training exposures of (background constant - exposure median) = 0, projected after every nuisance step; NIRCam stripes projected to zero mean over the rows / columns each exposure uses; (c) common shift: the LEARNED translations of the training exposures are projected to zero mean after every step (the initial registration shift0 is kept); all logged (gauge_report)

F19 geometry: Omega = (I + M_e)(X_wcs + shift0_e + D) + t_e about the BOX centre; D = tau_Ds Dst(det, xi, lambda) + tau_Dd Ddr(det, xi, t) + tau_De sum_j zD_ej B_j(xi) (6 fixed orthonormal quadratic fields, zD ~ N(0, I)); Dst / Ddr normalised over their references; shift0 from register_xcorr.json (LMC) or 0 (SMACS: the per-exposure translation is learned; the v31 coarse-shift code is not ported)

F20 sampling: patches of --patch-arcsec drawn uniformly plus --is-frac around local maxima of the current model band images above --is-snr (patch-level strata, exact 1/(N pi) reweighting: unbiased for the mean loss per pixel)

F21 variability scales: FUNCTION axes (kernel space / time / lambda, throughput space / time, static and drift distortion) by the held-out (validation) likelihood as a sequential evidence rule: one dither group per filter is carved out of training (--n-val-groups), its nuisances are fitted on one half of interleaved 4x4-pixel blocks, the gradient of the loss on the other half w.r.t. log tau is accumulated (--tau-accum), its exponential moving mean / sd (--tau-beta) give a significance z, and log tau moves by -lr_tau clip(z, -3, 3) while the axis is KEPT, i.e. while a likelihood-ratio check (held-out loss on the same validation patches with the axis switched off minus on, paired differences accumulated with forgetting --ab-beta) is significant at > --tau-occam-z sd, and shrinks geometrically otherwise (first order, no hypergradient; consecutive gradients are correlated, so z is optimistic; code-space kernel scales capped at --tau-code-max); RANDOM-EFFECT axes (kernel z_e, gain u_e, distortion zD_e) by a damped parameter-expanded EM step (tau <- tau x rms of the MAP effects; no posterior-variance term, so weakly constrained scales are biased low)

F22 detector: optional gated non-linearity (<= 20 per cent); background = quadratic Legendre per exposure + per-detector 8x8 bilinear pattern (zero mean) + NIRCam row/column stripes (L2 prior); no persistence, brighter-fatter, IPC or saturation model beyond the DQ mask

F23 noise sigma^2 = (sigma_pipe exp(h[det, filter]))^2 + (f_chan S)^2, h bounded +-3; Huber (delta 3) on z plus log sigma (Huber NLL not normalised); random-effect priors are divided by --prior-pixels (their weight against the per-pixel loss is a choice)
F24 optimisation: Adam; sky by --inner-sky steps per operator step (not an exact solve); warm-up + cosine on progress = max(step, time fraction); operator gradient clipping

F25 held-out exposures: ONLY per-exposure nuisances: first translation + background (--held-reg-steps, larger steps), then background, affine, gain u, codes z and zD, stripes by Adam on the exposure's own pixels (--held-steps), operator, sky and tau frozen; full-cut FFT render (phase 0), stripes re-solved in closed form (3 alternations); pixels within --pred-margin of the sky edge are not claimed (model_valid False)
F26 float32 throughout (positions relative to the box centre: ~1e-6 arcsec resolution); kernel activation checkpointing optional

F27 data: SCI/ERR/DQ of _cal; valid = DQ == 0, finite, ERR > 0, inside the data region; header (SIP) WCS through torchsky; epoch t normalised over the field's time span; epoch axes off when the training span < --epoch-min-days (SMACS: one day, so off)

F28 kernel warm start (physics only as a start): l fitted to log[0.85 N(sigma) + 0.15 Moffat(2 sigma, beta 1.5)], sigma^2 = (0.42 lambda/D)^2 + p^2/12, on random continuous offsets, with every variability term at zero; no PSF library, no STPSF
F29 (removed 18 Nov 2026): sky cross-fitting by dither-group fold (--xfit); the sky keeps its leading view axis of length 1 so saved states keep their shapes

F31 batched rendering (--batch-render): the patches of a step are rendered together per channel with ONE window size per level (the largest of the batch) and one random level-0 phase per batch; identical to the per-patch render to 5e-7 (values) / 3e-5 (gradients)
F30 instruments: the loader maps JWST NIRCam detectors; HST _flt/_flc loading through this package is not implemented yet

F32 several sky patches (--tiles): one operator, one sky per tile (each in the tangent plane of its own box centre), one row of per-exposure nuisances per exposure shared by its cuts in every tile; the per-exposure affine acts about the exposure's own reference point r_e in the FIELD frame (centroid of its valid pixels over all its cuts): Omega = x + M_e (x + c_k - r_e) + t_e with c_k the gnomonic offset of tile k's centre from the centroid of the selected boxes (about the field centroid instead, M_e had a 60-130 arcsec lever arm on LMC and each Adam step of M_e moved positions by ~10 mas); the north directions of two tile frames differ by dRA sin(dec) (0.13 deg across the LMC tiles), ignored in M_e (x + c_k - r_e) and t_e (effect < 0.2 mas for |M_e| < 1e-3)

F33 per-exposure metadata with several tiles (kernel frame R_e, sigbar, the reference median bkg0 of the pedestal gauge, pixel scale) come from the exposure's cut with most valid pixels; R_e of a cut in another tile differs by the frame rotation above (< 0.13 deg); the sky warm start of each tile subtracts that cut's own median

F34 tile schedule: visits of --visit-steps steps on one tile drawn with p_k proportional to (training pixels)^--tile-weight-power, so the objective is sum_k p_k L_k (per-pixel mean loss of tile k), the pooled pixel mean only for power 1; rows of exposures absent from a visit are not stepped (as F24); validation (tau) steps use the visited tile's validation cuts (no step on tiles without any)

F35 gauges with several skies: the common-shift projection acts per connected component of the (exposure, tile) training graph, the pedestal projection per (filter, component of that filter's graph); the throughput gauge stays global, so a sky scale of one component against the gains of its exposures is held only by the N(0, 1) prior on u_e (exposures shared across tiles tie the components together)

F36 data residency: pixel tensors of the cuts on the host (pinned), copied to the device per tile (LRU cache of --gpu-resident-gb); skies and their Adam states stay on the device (with --sky-swap they are moved to the host too when their tile is inactive); held-out nuisances are fitted cycling --held-rounds times over the tiles (shared rows), --held-steps scaled by held-out cuts / --held-ref-cuts per tile; each held-out cut is predicted with its tile's sky and the cuts are merged per exposure by the nearest tile centre (as stage3_blot); cuts are taken at REGISTERED positions (header + shift0)

F37 reference lattice and caps (12 Nov 2026, after the SMACS 200-min regression): the detector fields (kernel code, throughput, static / drift distortion) are normalised, and the throughput gauge is evaluated, on a 3x3 lattice at the cell centres of each detector's TRAINING footprint (bounding box of its valid training pixels; --ref-footprint 1), so each function-axis scale is the rms variation where the data are (on the fixed +-0.8 lattice, far outside the 20-arcsec SMACS footprint, the throughput scale ran away to 17.5 while the field varied by up to 1.9 in log g across the footprint); throughput scales are capped at --tau-g-max (rms log g) and static / drift distortion at --tau-d-max, because an axis kept by the likelihood-ratio check follows the validation gradient with no Occam pressure; the footprint is a bounding box (a box straddling a detector corner yields a lattice point without data)

F38 item sky (--sky-form items, 13 Nov 2026; default grid unchanged): s = sum_n [sum_k c_nk phi_k] G(. - x_n; Sigma_n); c_nk = exp(r_nk) > 0; widths sqrt(floor^2 + exp(2 l)) >= --item-floor (0 = 0.4 x sky pitch), capped at --item-max-width (0 = 16 x pitch). The items are RASTERISED on the SkyGrid coefficient grid at --sky-pitch and read by the unchanged renderers through the tent interpolant (so the sky is still a tent grid; the change is the parametrisation). Cell integral approximated by adding p^2/12 to both principal variances (the box replaced by an isotropic Gaussian of equal variance) and point-sampling, on a patch of +-4 effective widths, renormalised to exact flux (error before renormalisation 3 per cent at the floor, < 1e-3 above 1.5 x floor; per-node error vs the exact cell mean <= 2.2 per cent of the peak at the floor; sub-node centroid error <= 0.025 pitch); an item's rendered second moment is therefore at least 2 floor^2 + p^2/2 (0.82 p^2 at the default floor) against p^2/3 for one grid node; the blur gauge (F18) is unchanged and still set by one tent

F39 item seeding and updates: data-blind square lattices, level l (0 finest) holding a share 4^-l of --item-count (3 levels: 76/19/5 per cent), spacing 2 half / m, width half the spacing (>= floor), random angle, fine-level remainder on a Halton set; coefficients = level share x item area x max(warm-start coefficients smoothed at the item width, 1e-3 x their median peak); reseeded when the registration pre-pass rebuilds the warm start; Adam groups: positions --item-lr-pos x pitch, log widths, angles, log coefficients (their own steps, untuned, from the image-only experiment); the rasterised grid is cached while no sky parameter requires a gradient

F40 item pyramid rasteriser (--item-raster pyramid, 13 Nov 2026; default direct, bit-identical to F38): Gaussian semigroup. Level l has pitch p_l = 2^l p (level 0 = the sky grid); level l is carried to level l-1 by a fixed separable upsample-and-blur (stride-2 transposed convolution with a discretely normalised Gaussian of width s_l = p_l, taps +-5 s_l, flux conserved), so a level-l node arrives on the sky grid as a Gaussian of variance S_l^2 = sum_{j<=l} s_j^2 (sampling error of each step ~ exp(-2 pi^2 sigma_eff^2 / p_l^2), sigma_eff^2 >= p_l^2 / 2 for the first step). Item n (target covariance T_n = Sigma_n + p^2/12 I, as F38) goes to the coarsest level l whose remaining covariance T_n - S_l^2 I has its smaller principal width >= p_l (detached widths: a discrete switch; switch widths 2.81, 5.99, 12.2, 24.4, 48.9 ... sky pitches), and is point-sampled there with that covariance on +-4 larger remaining widths, normalised to exact flux; items below the level-1 threshold use the F38 path on the sky grid (with patch buckets extended from +-128 to +-512 nodes). Coarse grids extend beyond the sky grid by the cascade's reach, so items at or beyond the edge are right inside the grid; flux leaving the sky grid is dropped (as F38). Measured against an exact-flux point-sampled Gaussian of covariance T_n (larger width 0.5 to 200 nodes, axis ratios 1, 2, 5): worst node error 2.1e-4 of the peak (just above the level-1 switch; direct path 2.8e-4 from its +-4-width truncation, in its range), jump across a switch <= 2.3e-4 of the peak, flux exact to 2e-15. The number of levels follows from --item-max-width (allowed up to the field size). Cost per item depends on the item's axis ratio, not its size: with square patches an item costs (8 x larger remaining width / p_l)^2 nodes at the level set by its SMALLER width, so narrow elongated items stay on the sky grid at (larger width / p)^2; --item-patch sheared samples instead a box of +-4 widths in the item's decorrelated coordinates (rows along y, each row's columns centred on the conditional mean of x), ~ 64 sqrt(det) / p_l^2 nodes, used per item where it has 1.5x fewer nodes than the square, on every level including the sky grid (then level-0 items differ from F38 at the truncation level, <= 2.8e-4 of the peak). The patch layout (rounded centres, and with shearing each row's rounded column centre) is a discrete function of the detached parameters, so the raster jumps by up to ~exp(-8) of an item's peak where it changes (as F38 does when an item crosses a half node)

F41 flux convention of the kernel (--kernel-norm-radius R, 14 Nov 2026; default 0 = unit integral over the whole support, unchanged): with R > 0 the kernel's unit integral is taken inside R only (window 1 to 0.85 R, C1 fall to 0 at R), the kernel beyond R being free in amplitude. Reason: with the unit integral over the full +-10 arcsec support, a flat far pedestal of the kernel acting on the sky is absorbed by the background terms (per-detector pattern, quadratic terms), which nothing pins; the fitted SMACS sky then carries about 2 x the official mosaic's flux (1.7 to 4 depending on aperture) with 53 to 66 per cent of the kernel integral beyond +-32 pixels. With R the sky's flux scale is set by the light inside R: fluxes are 'inside R' fluxes, low against total-flux calibration by the true encircled fraction beyond R (NIRCam: about 1 to 3 per cent at 2 arcsec); the split between far wings and background stays unpinned but no longer moves the sky

F42 data-quality policy (--dq-ignore-bits B, 14 Nov 2026; default 0 = F27 unchanged): pixels whose only flags are among the bits B stay valid. Reason: the SMACS _cal files re-fetched from MAST on 13 Nov (CAL_VER 3.0.0, CRDS context 1584) flag the cores of the brightest sources SATURATED (bit 2: some groups saturated, slope fitted from the others) where the protocol's held-out masks, built from the earlier files with DQ == 0, call them valid; with strict DQ == 0 the fit never sees those cores and under-predicts them (0.84 of the data at reference S/N > 200 in one F277W exposure; chi2/N there 415 against 53). B = 2 keeps them; their slopes come from fewer groups, so they carry more non-linearity error than ERR states

F43 per-pixel gain (--pixel-gain detector | detector-filter, 16 Nov 2026; default off, bit-identical): d = N_e[G(p) S] + G(p) x (per-exposure quadratic background) + per-detector pattern + NIRCam stripes, G = exp(logg) per detector pixel p (one map per detector, or per detector and filter); the sky signal and the sky background pass through G, the pattern and the stripes (additive detector terms: residual dark, amplifier offsets, 1/f noise) do not; the non-linearity acts on G S (background excluded, as before); maps are allocated over the bounding box of the detector pixels valid in at least one TRAINING cut; pixels outside it or never observed in training (held-out pixels beyond the training footprint) get G = 1, i.e. no flat correction; one map per detector assumes a filter-independent pixel-to-pixel flat (official flats of one detector correlate at 0.98-0.99 between SW filters but only 0.85-0.90 between LW filters); with several tiles, cuts of one exposure that overlap on the detector are counted twice in the count / information maps (diagnostics only)

F44 gain gauge (exact, by projection after every gain step, no penalty, no prior): over the observed pixels of each map, logg is made orthogonal (uniform weights) to the monomials of total degree <= --pixel-gain-poly (default 2: mean, tilts, curvatures) of the pixel coordinates scaled to [-1, 1] over the box; this removes the mean (degenerate with the throughput and the per-exposure gains u_e) and the lowest-order smooth part (degenerate with the smooth throughput detector field and the quadratic backgrounds); smooth structure above degree 2 stays in the map, partly degenerate with the throughput detector field where that axis is on; no smoothness prior on the pixel-to-pixel part. Diagnostic stored with the map: information I_p = sum over training cuts of max(d^2 / sig^2 - 1, 0) (the Cramer-Rao bound 1 / sqrt(I_p) of logg if all else were known and m ~ d)

F45 gain optimisation: its own Adam (lr --lr-gain, default 3e-3 in log G, same warm-up + cosine factor as the operator, no gradient clipping), stepped in the joint step only, from progress --pixel-gain-start (0.1) on, so that the sky exists first; frozen in the held-out fit and in the validation steps. The step was chosen on the synthetic field (tests/synth_gain.py: 3e-4, 1e-3, 3e-3, 1e-2 scanned, about 130 gradient visits per pixel in 200 steps); a SMACS pixel gets only ~30-35 visits in a 200-minute fit, so the map may be under-converged there. Adam's momentum moves pixels between visits (no row masking as for per-exposure nuisances)

F46 _rate input (--input-level rate): SCI / ERR / DQ from the _rate file (DN/s; ERR without the flat-field variance; DQ without the NO_FLAT_FIELD bit the _cal adds), header WCS and PIXAR_A2 from the SCI header of the matching _cal file (--rate-wcs cal, default): the _rate header has only the linear TAN WCS of the pointing (0.07 arcsec median, 0.24 arcsec maximum from the _cal SIP WCS over NRCB1); the WCS is a geometric step of calwebb_image2, kept, while flat field and photometric conversion are not applied; predictions are written in DN/s with meta units = 'rate' (score_paired.py --level rate converts calibrated-unit predictions with C = rate / cal)
